notes: Commissioned lore (soak order 2026-08-09): the -லாம் tail as a MACHINE, not three phrases. The tail is spoken bare (லாம்) and then bolted onto six verbs — கிளம்ப / சாப்பிட / போ / உட்கார / பேச / பார்க்க — before any payload chunk is named, so the pattern is the payload. Three senses carved in order: suggestion → +ஆ question → permission (நான் வெளிய போலாமா?). The paakkalaam/pakkam minimal pair is delivered by PARTS, not repetition: பார்த்தேன் (already cold-adjacent for him) exposes the பார் at the front of பார்க்கலாம், the fast-mouth collapse to பாக்கலாம் is named explicitly (ர் eaten, long ஆ stays), and பக்கம் is counted out as two flat beats with no ஆ and no பார். The auto example reproduces his own live error verbatim in the third person: 'temple பக்கத்துல நிறுத்துங்க' (a stop) vs 'temple பாக்கலாம்' (an outing). பக்கத்துல taught as the form he actually needed. Zero unfenced Tamil — every non-payload noun the scene needed is carried in English (traffic, bags, door, temple, bus stop, coffee), which is what a Coimbatore hall sounds like anyway. PRODUCTION NOTE FOR THE NEXT PRODUCER: render_audio.py's parser turns ANY line containing [Pause: N sec] into a pause and discards that line's speech, so every pause here is on its own line — M74 lost real dialogue to inline pauses and the loss is invisible in the script.
